Embark on the Kanchenjunga Complete Circuit Trek. Explore both North and South Base Camps on Nepal's ultimate remote 21-day trekking adventure.

The Trail Conditions:

Straight, Uphill, Downhill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, somewhere flat man made stone steps, through the rhododendron, moss covered forests, suspensions metal bridges

Medication

  • Bandage for sprains
  • Plasters/Band-aids
  • Iodine or water filter (optional)
  • Moleskin/Second skin - for blisters
  • Antiseptic ointment for cuts
  • Anti-bacterial throat lozenges (with antiseptic)
  • Aspirin/paracetamol - general painkiller
  • Oral dehydration salts
  • Broad-spectrum antibiotic (norfloxacin or ciprofloxin)
  • Anti-diarrhea medication (antibiotic)
  • Diarrhea stopper (Imodium - optional)
  • Antibiotic for Giardia or similar microbe or bacteria
  • Diamox (altitude sickness - can be bought in Kathmandu)

 

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing / equipment for our trek to Rara Lake

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket
  • Set lightweight thermals
  • North Face down Jacket (Preferably)
  • Small thin towel (sports towel best)
  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
  • Hat
  • Cotton or silk bag liner – optional
  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves
  • Rucksack
  • Pack tissues
  • Pair sunglasses
  • Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.
  • Camera and films
  • Head torch and spare batteries
  • Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) deg C during our trek)

Above things are required for Rara Lake Trek. However if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.

Nar Phu Valley Trek & Thorong La Pass
Explore the Nar Phu Valley Trek with a challenging Thorong La Pass crossing, remote villages, Tibetan culture, and breathtaking Himalayan scenery.

The Trail Conditions:

Straight, Uphill, Downhill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, somewhere flat man made stone steps, through the rhododendron, moss covered forests, suspensions metal bridges

Medication

  • Bandage for sprains
  • Plasters/Band-aids
  • Iodine or water filter (optional)
  • Moleskin/Second skin - for blisters
  • Antiseptic ointment for cuts
  • Anti-bacterial throat lozenges (with antiseptic)
  • Aspirin/paracetamol - general painkiller
  • Oral dehydration salts
  • Broad-spectrum antibiotic (norfloxacin or ciprofloxin)
  • Anti-diarrhea medication (antibiotic)
  • Diarrhea stopper (Imodium - optional)
  • Antibiotic for Giardia or similar microbe or bacteria
  • Diamox (altitude sickness - can be bought in Kathmandu)

Clothing / Equipment List

Kindly bring the following list of clothing / equipment for our trek to Upper Dolpo Trek

  • Pair trekking boots and waterproofing agent
  • Pair lightweight trekking sandals
  • Pairs thin walking socks
  • Pairs lightweight wind – water proof pants
  • T-shirts
  • Fleece Jacket
  • Set lightweight thermals
  • North Face down Jacket (Preferably)
  • Small thin towel (sports towel best)
  • Soap
  • Shampoo
  • Sunscreen
  • Extra lightweight shirt for daypacks - for stops along the way
  • Hat
  • Cotton or silk bag liner – optional
  • Neck warmer
  • Pairs 'thinners' gloves
  • Rucksack
  • Pack tissues
  • Pair sunglasses
  • Water filter / Iodine (you could buy boiled water in hotels/ lodges which is safe to drink.
  • Camera and films
  • Head torch and spare batteries
  • Sleeping bag (rated -15(above) deg C during our trek)

Above things are required for Upper Dolpo trek. However if you do not have clothing you can either buy or rent in Nepal. In this case we have equipment cheaper than your country.
Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, you will be warmly welcomed and transferred to your hotel. Enjoy a brief orientation about the trek and rest after your journey.
Sightseeing / Cultural Day In Kathmandu Valley

Explore the rich cultural heritage of Kathmandu Valley. Visit UNESCO World Heritage Sites including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Pashupatinath Temple, Boudhanath Stupa, and Patan Durbar Square. Prepare for your upcoming trek in the evening.
Take a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, a vibrant city in western Nepal close to the Indian border. Overnight in Nepalgunj.
Fly from Nepalgunj to Jumla (2,370m), a remote and picturesque town in the highlands of western Nepal. Begin acclimatizing to the higher altitude.
Start trekking through lush forests and traditional villages to reach Gothi Chaur. Enjoy the beautiful landscape and gradual ascent.
Continue your trek through alpine meadows, passing by yak pastures and scattered settlements, eventually reaching Naphuknona.
Descend into the Bheri River Valley, following the scenic trail alongside the river. Take in the dramatic gorges and untouched wilderness.
Trek through traditional villages and diverse landscapes to reach Hurikot, a gateway to the Upper Dolpo region and Shey Phoksundo National Park.
Continue your journey deeper into the remote mountains, reaching the beautiful Garpung Khola valley where you’ll camp near the river.
We start the trek following the river upstream.
Begin the day by trekking upstream along the Garpung Khola. The trail winds through pristine valleys, offering breathtaking views and tranquil surroundings.

A big day crossing the Kagmara La (5100m). Taking a packed lunch, follow the Right Bank off the river for a short way until the path becomes slightly obscure below a steep climb. Reaching the top of this, the angle eases off slightly and the pass is no more than an hour and a half away. The pass is marked in the traditional Tibetan way with hundreds of prayer flags, and the view is quite stunning. The short climb to the summit of Kagmara RI (5370m) takes no more than half an hour, but the extra view is well worth it. The mountains of Tibet and Mount Everest in the distance form just part of this impressive panorama, which is dominated by the Dhaulagiri massif and the Annapurnas. The view to the south and west of the Kagmara Lekh and the Kanjiroba Himal is equally impressive. All in all a very special spot. There is no need to leave in a hurry, as the campsite is a mere hour below the pass on a flat grassy clearing by the river (3450m).

On our 1990 reconnaissance trip, Himalayan blue sheep and wild fox ware seen from the camp as well s numerous birds of pray. A big descent, over 1200 meters, leads through an idyllic valley to the village of Pungmo. Camp is made by the Choten the entrance to the village.

A rest day if you wish, but the spare day is to give everyone the chance to visit the important Gompa above Pungmo. There are in fact two Gompas as we have entered a region where both 'Bon' and 'traditional' Buddhism are practiced. Chotens become very confusing s one dictates an anti- clockwise passing whilst the other clockwise. However, the lams of both Gompas are willing to show you around for a small donation. To reach them, look out for a wooden bridge below the village. Cross this to the opposite bank of the river and follow the path up through the pine forest past a Choten. The path becomes quite exposed as it cuts across a cliff to reach the sanctuary

Today's destination is the village of Ringmo by the beautiful Phuksumdo Tal (lake). Keeping to the left side of the river, descend for one hour to a military camp (31d50m) at the junction of the Pungmo and Phuksumdo Rivers. Turns left immediately after the camp and follow a delightful path by the Phuksumdo River to a grassy clearing for lunch. The afternoon's walk up to Ringmo is very rewarding as huge rock walls guard the upper valley and it is not until some prayer flags are reached at 3800m that the lake can be seen. Equally impressive is the huge waterfall falling down from the Phuksumdo River. From the prayer flags, a pleasant half an hour's walk leads to the village of Ringmo and camp is made on the opposite side of the village (3700m). Crossing the bridge in the village and turn left to reach the lake.
A rest day in Ringmo camped by the beautiful clear waters of Ringmo Lake. The nearby monastery is worth a visit.

The final part of the trek sets out to explore the hidden valley of Tarap, one of the last bastions of Tibetan culture in Nepal. An easy day involving a couple of hours walks in the morning to a Yak grazing pasture by the Manduwa Khola. The path skirts along lodges hacked out of cliffs for the Yak caravans from Dolpo. The views down the Suli Gad and across to the Kagmara Lekh are particularly impressive. The campsite is in a lovely spot (3900m) below Kang Taiga (5916m).

Today is a very strenuous day crossing thee Basic Bhanjyang (Bagar La) (5200m). It is also one of the most fascination of the trek as we cross the watershed of the main Himalayan onto the dry Tibetan plateaus. Following the river to begin with, the path turns north up the first obvious side valley and climbs steeply to the pass, which marked by a choten and the usual prayer flags. The views to the east and north are one of complete contrast to those of the previous two weeks trekking. The mountain is orange and brown stretching out into Tibet to the north. The pass is often windy and the descent is party rapid to the river below and our camp (4650m). The road to shey and saldang is clearly etched out of the landscape by the tracks of thousands of Yaks that have made the journey south over the centuries the lifeline of Dolpo. At this point we are only three hours from the village of Shey, but access is not permitted.

The Tarap Valley is today's destination and despite the climb to the Numla La (5350m), the walk into this beautiful and wild Tibetan landscape is one of the highlights of the trek. A four to five hour climb leads to the pass and the view is indeed stunning. Dhaulagiri I am the prominent feature, with the rolling Tibetan hills and the Kanjiroba Himal to the west equally impressive. For an excellent 3600 panorama, climb the small peak to the left of the pass. The path descends gradually into the Tarap Valley. In two to three hours the Champa Gompa is passed on the left and camp is made a little further down the valley in the first village (4300m).

A long day. Due to the opens of the Tarap Valley, the sun hits the tent early, giving a spring feel to the morning. The mornings walk passes through the villages off Clumaga and Kakar, both extremely interesting with many Choten, again both Bun-Po (the ancient pre-Buddhistic religion) and Choba (orthodox Buddhist). There are two Gompas in Dho, Guru Bumba (Chob) and above the village Scipcha Gompa (Bon). Leaving Dho (a name given to the last village but actually meaning the upper collection of villages), the Tarap Khola is followed for two hours, at first on its left bank, to a bridge where lunch is taken. This is the last flat ground for three to four hours as the valley becomes narrow with deep goes crossed by innumerable small bridges. However, it is an extremely well made path, one of the finest gorge paths in the Himalayan, offering an entertaining afternoon's walk. A small campsite by a large campsite by a big cave.

The path through the gorge continues to impress, switching from the riverbank to way up the cliff side on some amazing constructions! After a long morning's walk (look out for Musk Deer), a large clearing by the river is reached. This is Lahini and marks the end of the gorge. The path Kanigaon (2700m) where we camp.

From the check post, head east for a few hundred yards to a well mad bridge which is crossed to the left bank of the Barbung Khola, into which the Trap Khola now flows. This river is followed for three hours to the village of Tarakot where we stop. Rest afternoon.
Another easy day, continuing along the Barbung Khola through a beautiful alpine valley to the Hindu village of Dunai. Four hours walking. Camp by the new 'Blue Sheep lodge'.

The final day's walk continues along the river to a tea shop by the side of the path (One and a half hours) which marks the start of the climb to the Juphal airstrip. The path climbs steadily, passing through the village of Juphal to the airstrip. Camp is made outside the RNAC office.
We take the flight to Nepalgunj, for an afternoon's rest before flying on to Kathmandu the following day. The views from the lake of the Annapurnas are famous throughout Nepal.

High Altitude Sickness:

Often times treks that ascend beyond 3500 m would require more days for acclimatization to ensure that trekkers do not suffer from high altitude sickness. The thinner air affects you in many ways and if you go high too fast there is a high chance to get affected.

Insurances of Guide and Porters

We do our Trekking insurance for the duration of 10 or 15 years from reputed insurance company in Kathmandu, Nepal which covers our insurance for the duration of our trek as well. On the other hand we (Hike Nepal) are a member of TAAN (Trekking Agent Association of Nepal) TAAN takes fully responsible for the staff of its members while we are on the trek. You are highly recommended to be insured for this trek from your country.

We, Nepalese eat a meal of Dhal Bhaat (rice with lentil soup, curry, and pickles) twice daily. The ingredients vary according to local and seasonal availability, but vegetarian options are the norm. Another cheap popular local dish is the ubiquitous instant noodle soup, enhanced by local vegetables, or meat or egg, depending on availability. Eating Nepali-style will provide you with truly local experience, guarantees fresh ingredients everywhere, and rules out disappointments.

Also, in all lodges tourists will be served their meals in the lodge dining room before the Nepali staff gets their meals in the kitchen or another place where guides and porters relax. And staff members' quarters are separate from the tourist rooms. This seemingly two-class system may be a difficult concept for some tourists, but it can also be seen as "time off" for the staff members. Nepalese eat mostly with their hands, a custom that is considered offensive by some tourists another reason why the staff members may actually prefer to eat separately.

Classic Everest Trek from Jiri - Everpeak Adventure
Follow history on the Classic Everest Trek from Jiri. Explore the original pioneer route to Everest Base Camp through authentic villages and alpine forests.

The Trail Conditions

Straight, Up hill, Down hill, Jig Jag with small rocky, pebbles, muddy, some where dusty, man made stone steps, through the moss covered forests, Rocky glacier or If snows, snowy path crossing suspensions metal bridges and wooden bridges over the rivers

High Altitude Sickness:

Often times treks that ascends beyond 3500 m would require more days for acclimatization to ensure that trekkers do not suffer from high altitude sickness. The thinner air affects you in many ways and if you go high too fast there is a high chance to get effect.

Insurances of Guide and Porters

We do our Trekking insurance for the duration of 10 or 15 years from reputed insurance company in Kathmandu, Nepal which covers our insurance for the duration of our trek as well. On the other hand we (Himalayana Nomad Trek are member of TAAN (Trekking Agent Association of Nepal) TAAN takes fully responsible for the staffs of its members while we are on the trek. You are highly recommended to be insured for this trek from your country.

We, Nepalese eat a meal of Dhal Bhaat (rice with lentil soup, curry and  pickles) twice daily. The ingredients vary according to local and seasonal availability, but vegetarian options are the norm. Another cheap popular local dish is the ubiquitous instant noodle soup, enhanced by local vegetables, or meat or egg, depending on availability.. Eating Nepali-style will provide you with a truly local experience, guarantees fresh ingredients everywhere, and rules out disappointments.

Also, in all lodges tourists will be served their meals in the lodge dining room before the Nepali staff gets their meals in the kitchen or another place where guides and porters relax. And staff members' quarters are separate from the tourist rooms. This seemingly two-class system may be a difficult concept for some tourists, but it can also be seen as "time off" for the staff members. Nepalese eat mostly with their hands, a custom that is considered offensive by some tourists another reason why the staff members may actually prefer to eat separately.

Annapurna Base Camp Trek: Complete 12-Day Guide
Embark on the iconic Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Our 12-day itinerary offers stunning Himalayan views, rich local culture, and an unforgettable adventure.

Key Highlights of the Everest Panorama Trek

  • Scenic mountain flight from Kathmandu to Lukla with spectacular Himalayan views.

  • Trek through the pristine landscapes of Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site rich in natural beauty.

  • Explore Namche Bazaar, the vibrant Sherpa capital and cultural hub of the Everest region.

  • Panoramic viewpoints from the famous Everest View Hotel.

  • Stunning views of iconic Himalayan peaks including Mount Everest, Ama Dablam, and Lhotse.

  • Immersive Sherpa culture with monasteries, prayer flags, mani stones, and traditional teahouse hospitality.

  • Moderate altitude (around 3,880 meters) with lower risk of altitude sickness compared to Everest Base Camp.

  • Ideal short trek (7–10 days) suitable for beginners, families, and travelers with limited time.

• Scenic drive from Pokhara to Jhinu, followed by a beautiful trek into the Annapurna region

  • Reach Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 meters) surrounded by stunning Himalayan peaks

  • Enjoy close views of Annapurna I, Machapuchhre (Fishtail), Hiunchuli, and Annapurna South

  • Experience traditional Gurung and Magar villages, including the famous Chhomrong village

  • Walk through lush forests filled with bamboo, waterfalls, and rhododendron trees

  • Explore the peaceful and breathtaking Annapurna Sanctuary glacial valley

  • Witness unforgettable sunrise and sunset views over snow-covered mountains

  • Stay in traditional mountain teahouses and experience local hospitality

  • Opportunity to see wildlife such as langur monkeys, Himalayan thar, and colorful birds

  • Short and rewarding trek suitable for trekkers with limited time but big Himalayan dreams

  • Experience a complete journey from green hills to high alpine mountain landscapes in just six days

Pokhara – Samrung – Sinuwa (2,200m / 7,218ft) (3 hrs Jeep, 4 hrs trek)

Start your journey early from Lakeside, Pokhara, taking a scenic jeep ride to Samrung via Nayapul (approx. 3 hours). Enjoy breathtaking views of the Seti River, Modi River, rolling green hills, and traditional villages along the way. From Samrung, begin your trek toward Sinuwa, a peaceful village surrounded by lush forests and stunning mountain vistas. The trek takes around 4 hours, with gentle ascents through terraced fields and charming settlements. Experience the warmth of local hospitality as you settle in for the night in a cozy teahouse in Sinuwa.

Today’s journey takes you deeper into the Himalayas as you trek from Sinuwa to Deurali. The trail winds through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests, offering glimpses of snow-capped peaks along the way. As you ascend, the air gets cooler, and the landscapes become more rugged and dramatic. After 7 hours of trekking, arrive at Deurali, a serene village nestled beneath towering cliffs. Relax and recharge for the next day's exciting adventure to Annapurna Base Camp. You’ll be staying in a cozy teahouse in Deurali for the night.
Deurali – Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m / 13,550ft) (6 hrs trek)

Embark on the most thrilling day of the trek as you make your way from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC). The trail ascends gradually, leading you past glacial moraines and high-altitude landscapes. After 5 hours of trekking, you’ll reach the legendary Annapurna Base Camp, surrounded by towering peaks and pristine glaciers. Marvel at the panoramic views of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and Hiunchuli. Spend the night at Annapurna Base Camp itself, soaking in the beauty of the Himalayas under a starry sky.
Annapurna Base Camp – Lower Sinuwa (2,200m / 7,218ft) (8 hrs trek

Wake up early to witness a spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna Massif before beginning your descent. Retrace your steps back through Deurali and Bamboo, passing through diverse landscapes of alpine meadows and dense forests. The trek to Lower Sinuwa takes around 8 hours, offering plenty of time to reflect on your incredible journey. Enjoy a well-earned rest in a cozy teahouse, surrounded by the tranquil beauty of the region
Lower Sinuwa – Jhinu Dada Hot Springs – Pokhara (4 hrs trek, 3 hrs drive)

On the final day, descend from Lower Sinuwa to Jhinu Dada (4 hours of trekking). Treat yourself to a relaxing dip in the natural hot springs, soothing your tired muscles and celebrating your trekking achievement. Afterward, take a 3-hour jeep ride back to Lakeside, Pokhara, enjoying the scenic drive through picturesque villages and lush hills. Arrive in Pokhara with unforgettable memories, a deep appreciation for the Annapurna region, and a sense of accomplishment from your adventure. On the way, reflect on the incredible experiences, stunning landscapes, and the sense of achievement you've gained throughout the journey

Pokhara/Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani(1800m/5,905 ft) (8/9 hrs drive)
You'll be driven from Pokhara/Kathmandu to Besisahar on a bus and then you'll be continuing your journey toward Dharapani on a shared Jeep enjoying the scenic journey.
Dharapani to Chame (2,670m/8,760 ft)(10 hrs drive) (6 hrs trek)

You'll then be trekking up in the mountains from Dharapani until reaching Chame enjoying the beauty of the himalayan range. This is just the beginning of the trek. You’ll be staying overnight at teahouse at Chame.
Chame to Upper Pisang (3,300m/10,826 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Chame to Upper Pisang, a picturesque village with stunning mountain views. You'll explore and immerse yourself in the local culture
Upper Pisang to Ngawal (3,700m/12,140 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll continue the trek to Ngawal, a beautiful village nestled in a hillside. The breathtaking views of Annapurna II, Annapurna III, and Gangapurna mountains and valleys will mesmerize you.
Ngawal to Manang(3540m/11,614 ft)(Acclimatization Day)(2 hrs trek)

You'll trek to Manang after exploring the cave nearby Ngawal and take a day to rest and acclimatize to the higher altitude in Manang. You will explore the village and enjoy the panoramic mountain views.
Manang to Yak Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. You'll prepare for the challenging pass-crossing the next day. Overnight stay in Thorong Phedi..
Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi (4,450m/14,600 ft)(6 hrs trek)
You'll trek from Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. You'll prepare for the challenging pass-crossing the next day. Overnight stay in Thorong Phedi.
Thorong Phedi to Muktinath (3,800m/12,467 ft) via Thorong La Pass (5,416m/17,769 ft)(12 hrs trek)

You'll start early in the morning for the challenging but rewarding ascent to Thorong La Pass. You'll experience the thrill of crossing the high mountain pass and enjoy panoramic views. You'll descend to Muktinath temple, a sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and explore the scenic village. Overnight stay in Muktinath..
Muktinath to Jomsom (2,720m/8,923 ft)(5 hrs trek)

You'll descend further to Jomsom, a windy town in the Mustang region. You'll witness the dramatic change in landscapes as you enter the arid and desert-like terrain and explore the town. Overnight stay in Jomsom.

You'll take a bus from Jomsom to Pokhara, enjoying views of the mountains. You'll relax and unwind in Pokhara, reflecting on the incredible journey you've completed. Congratulation! You've accomplished your dream adventure.

We will begin our journey with a morning drive right after breakfast that will lead you to Syabrubesi. The bus journey follows a winding route, navigating both uphill and downhill roads, passing through various rural towns and farming villages. Along the way, you will encounter Trisuli Bazaar, a larger town situated in the sub-tropical zone in Nuwakot district. As the road ascends further, transitioning into a cooler region, the landscape changes from rice paddies to terraced fields of maize and millet. With these changes in weather and environment come shifts in culture and people as well. Eventually, you will arrive at Dhunche (1,965 m.), which serves as the primary town of both the Langtang area and Rasuwa district. Here lies Langtang National Park headquarters where your trekking permits are thoroughly checked by park wardens from the Royal Nepalese Army who are responsible for overseeing this protected area. Continuing your journey downhill for approximately 1-2 hours brings you to Syabrubesi village where we will stay for the night.
Syabrubesi - Bamboo - Lama Hotel (6 hrs trek)

The journey from Syabrubeshi is quite enjoyable, with a few uphill sections. However, the majority of the hike takes place on a relatively flat trail that passes through terraced farm fields and villages. Eventually, the trail descends and merges with another path that originates from upper Syabru at the Riverside Lodge. From there, you continue along a path that leads into a refreshing forest within the gorge, following alongside the rushing Trisuli River. The trek mainly consists of climbing uphill in the pleasant shade of rhododendron and oak forests. After approximately six hours of hiking, you reach a small clearing where Lama Hotel is situated. You will spend overnight at Teahouse/Lodge accommodations
Lama Hotel - Langtang Village (6 hrs trek)

Starting from Lama Hotel, a morning hike of 2-3 hours will take you to Ghoda btable. Ghodatabela is situated in the midst of a forest filled with pine, hemlock, and rhododendron trees. As you continue on this trail, you will begin to notice the effects of increasing altitude. In Nepali language, Ghoda tabela means "horse stable." In the past, people from Langtang and even as far as Kathmandu used to trade with Tibet by bringing Tibetan ponies to this town. Ghoda tabela was an ideal place for cattle and horses to graze. Upon reaching Ghoda tabela, there is a lodge and a park warden's barrack where your permit will be checked once again. From here onward, the trek continues for a few more hours along the trail leading to Langtang and its picturesque valley. For about an hour after leaving Ghoda tabela behind, you walk through refreshing shade provided by alpine woods while following a small stream. As you ascend uphill for another hour or so before reaching Langtang village itself via gentle winding trails that have occasional ups and downs.

Starting from Mundu, the morning stroll takes you along a flat path for a brief period before gradually ascending through thorny blueberry and alpine bushes. Along the way, you will come across a Mani prayer wall that should be circumvented in a clockwise direction, adhering to local customs and beliefs. As you continue eastward, the valley opens up and reveals a grassy meadow offering breathtaking views of numerous snowcovered peaks in the distance. The journey becomes more enjoyable but may feel more challenging due to the gain in altitude as you approach Kyanjin Gompa for your overnight stay. Situated amidst picturesque surroundings, Kyanjin Gompa is adorned with towering peaks visible from all directions. Among them is Langtang Lirung, reaching an impressive height of over 7,000 meters with its icefall not too far from the village. Perched on top of a ridge created by glacial debris consisting of rocks and boulders lies Kyanjin Gompa monastery—a small sanctuary within an area that also includes more than 20 lodges and even a cheese factory. This stretch of the trek takes about 3 hours. You will have your lunch ready upon reaching Kyanjin Gompa. If the weather is permissible, you will then be guided towards Kyanjin Ri which takes about 3 hours roundtrip. Upon returning spend your night at Teahouse/Lodge accommodations.
Kyanjin Gomba - Langtang Village - Thangshyap (6 hrs trek)

As per the itinerary plan you will start your return journey after a pleasant night at Kyanjin Gompa. If the weather on the previous day is not feasible, you will be taking a morning hike to the top of Kyanjin ri on this day. After returning from the hike, you will be served with breakfast before your beginning your return journey. The trail we take is the same on our way up. We traverse descending through small hamlets located along. Further ahead from Langtang Village, we reach Thangshyap for our night stay
Thangshyap - Lama Hotel - Rimche - Bamboo - Syabrubesi (6 hrs trek)

We retrace our footsteps alongside Langtang Khola towards Syabrubesi. Today’s stretch is all descent that is steep and through dense forest. We traverse through Bamboo and Pairo villages before reaching the Langtang hydropower project. From here we walk on a dirt road towards Syabrubesi marking the end of our trekking journey. Overnight at Syabrubesi hotel.

On the final day, our vehicle will start off from Syabrubesi for your drive towards Kathmandu. We will take the high mountains road of Rasuwa and descend to Nuwakot. From Nuwakot, its a smooth sailing highway ride towards Kathmandu. It takes anywhere from 6-7 hours to reach Kathmandu. We will drop you off at your hotel in the evening. Arrive at your hotel with unforgettable memories, a deep appreciation for the Langtang region, and a sense of accomplishment from your adventure. Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani (1800m/5,905 ft) - Chame (2,670m/8,760 ft) (10 hrs drive)
You will be taken by a bus from Kathmandu to Besisahar and then continue your journey to Dharapani and finally to Chame in a private Jeep, enjoying the scenic journey.
Chame to Upper Pisang (3,300m/10,826 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Chame, you'll walk to Upper Pisang, a picturesque village with stunning mountain views. You will discover and immerse yourself in the local culture.
Upper Pisang to Ngawal (3,700m/12,140 ft) (6 hrs hike)
You will continue the hike to Ngawal, a beautiful village located on a hillside. The breathtaking views of Annapurna II, Annapurna III, and Gangapurna mountains and valleys will mesmerize you.
After exploring the cave near Ngawal, you will walk to Manang and take a day to relax and get used to the high altitude in Manang. You will explore the village and enjoy panoramic mountain views.
Manang - Tilicho Base Camp (4,150m/13,615 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Manang, you will hike to Tilicho Base Camp. You will soar through the alpine landscapes and experience the tranquility of the high Himalayas.
Tilicho Base Camp to Shri Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft) (6 hrs hike)

From the Base Camp, you will walk to Lake Tilicho (5050m/16,568 ft) and enjoy the natural beauty of the tranquil lake surrounded by mountains. You'll rise and fall through the Alpine landscapes and experience the high Himalayas.
Shri Kharka - Yak Kharka (4,050m/13,287 ft) (6 hrs walk)
You will walk from Shri Kharka to Yak Kharka and experience the natural beauty of the Manang and Annapurna Himalayas.
Yak Kharka - Thorong Phedi (4,450m/14,600 ft) (6 hrs hike)
From Yak Kharka, you will walk to Thorong Phedi, the base camp for the Thorong La Pass. The next day, you will be prepared for the difficult passage of passage.
Thorong Phedi to Muktinath (3,800m/12,467 ft) via Thorong La Pass (5,416m/17,769 ft) (12 hrs walk)

You'll set off early in the morning for the challenging but rewarding climb to Thorong La Pass. You will experience the thrill of crossing the high mountain pass and enjoy the panoramic views. You will descend to the Muktinath temple, a sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and explore the scenic village. Overnight stay will be in Muktinath.

You'll descend towards Jomsom, a windswept town in the Mustang district. You'll witness the dramatic change in landscapes as you venture into the arid and desert-like terrain and explore the town and head towards Tatopani Hotspring where you’ll take a dip into Natural Hotspring to rejuvenate yourself. Overnight stay will be in Tatopani.

You will be driven from Tatopani to Pokhara and enjoy the mountain views. You will relax and unwind thinking about the incredible journey you have completed in Pokhara. Congratulations! You've completed your dream adventure.

Proper equipment and trekking gear are essential for a safe and comfortable Everest Base Camp Trek. Since the trek passes through different altitudes and weather conditions, having the right clothing and gear helps you stay warm, dry, and protected throughout the journey.

Clothing should be layered to adjust easily to changing temperatures. A moisture-wicking base layer, warm fleece or down jacket, and a waterproof outer jacket are highly recommended. Comfortable trekking pants, thermal innerwear, gloves, warm hat, and wool socks are also important, especially at higher elevations where temperatures drop significantly.

Good quality trekking boots are one of the most important items. They should be well-fitted, waterproof, and already broken in before the trek to avoid blisters. A lightweight daypack is needed to carry daily essentials such as water, snacks, camera, and extra clothing.

Other essential items include sunglasses with UV protection, sunscreen, lip balm, reusable water bottle, trekking poles, and a sleeping bag suitable for cold temperatures. Personal items such as basic toiletries, medications, and a headlamp are also necessary.

Choosing the right gear ensures comfort, safety, and confidence, allowing you to fully enjoy the Everest Base Camp trekking experience.

The‌ Manaslu region is home to a mix of Gurung, Nubri, and Tibetan-influenced communities‍, each with their own traditi‌ons, dialects, and way‍ o‍f life. Ma‍ny villages,‍ especially at higher altitudes like Samagaon and Samdo, follow strong Budd‌h‌is‌t practic‌e‍s. You‌’l‌l find prayer flags, maniwa‌lls (stone carvings with Buddhist prayers),‌ and monasteries througho‌ut the trek. Life here is simp‌le and‌ revolves around farming, herding yaks, and religious rituals.

As a visitor, showing respect‍ to loca‍l culture is very important. Always walk to the le‌ft side o‌f maniwalls and stupas as a sign of respect, and spin prayer⁠ whe‍el‌s clockwise. Greet locals with a smile and a simple‍ “‌Na‍maste‍” or the Tibetan‍ greeting “Tashi Delek.” Modest dress is app‌reciated in‍ villages cover shoulder‍s and avoid very short clothing, even though trek‍king gear is acce‌ptable.

What we can do

Walk left of s‌tupa‌s (clockwise).

Greet locals with Namaste or‍ Tashi Delek.

D‍ress modestly in villages.

Carry your trash and keep the trail clean.

Hike slo‌wly and acclimati‍ze pr‍operly.

Support local tea houses and‍ buy from villagers.

‌Ask before taking photos.

What we can't do

Don’t touch a‍ny‌one’s head or point your feet at shrines.

Don’t enter monasteries withou‍t per‌mission.

Don’t harm animals or w‍ildlif‌e.

Don’t litter or leave plastic waste behind.

Explore the Manaslu Circuit Trek through remote villages, dramatic Himalayan landscapes, rich local culture, and the challenging Larke La Pass.

• Trek through the beautiful Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's most scenic Himalayan regions.
  • Summit Yala Peak (5,500m), a perfect introductory trekking peak.
  • Enjoy breathtaking views of Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Shishapangma, and surrounding Himalayan peaks.
  • Visit the traditional Tamang villages and experience local mountain culture.
  • Explore the historic settlement of Kyanjin Gompa.
  • Hike to Kyanjin Ri for spectacular sunrise and panoramic mountain views.
  • Walk through lush forests of rhododendron, pine, and bamboo.
  • Encounter diverse wildlife within Langtang National Park.
  • Experience comfortable teahouse accommodation throughout the trek.
  • Ideal combination of cultural trekking and non-technical peak climbing adventure.

Upper Mustang Trek – 16 Days via lo manthang
Explore the Upper Mustang Trek on a 16-day journey with scenic drives, ancient monasteries, desert landscapes, and two nights in historic Lo Manthang.
Hotels in Kathmandu and teahouses during the trek

• Explore the remote and sacred Tsum Valley, often called the “Hidden Valley of Happiness”
  • Visit ancient Buddhist monasteries like Mu Gompa and Rachen Gompa
  • Experience authentic Tibetan-influenced culture and traditional village life
  • Scenic drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola through rivers, hills, and valleys
  • Trek through untouched landscapes of the Manaslu Conservation Area
  • Walk along beautiful Budhi Gandaki River with suspension bridges and deep gorges
  • Spot diverse Himalayan flora, fauna, and peaceful alpine scenery
  • Reach high viewpoints with dramatic views of Manaslu and surrounding peaks

• All airport pick-up and drop-off in Kathmandu
  • 3 nights hotel accommodation in Kathmandu with breakfast
  • Full board meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) during the trek
  • Licensed English-speaking trekking guide

Explore the Chum Valley Trek on a 16-day Himalayan adventure featuring ancient monasteries, remote villages, dramatic landscapes, and stunning mountain views.

• Trek through the remote Manaslu region, home to the world’s 8th highest peak, Manaslu (8,163 m).

• Explore the off-the-beaten-path Chum Valley, rich in Tibetan Buddhist culture and traditional mountain villages.

• Experience stunning Himalayan panoramas, including views of Manaslu, Himalchuli, Ganesh Himal, and Annapurna ranges.

• Cross the Larkya La Pass (5,160 m), a thrilling high-altitude pass offering spectacular landscapes.

• Visit ancient Buddhist monasteries, mani walls, and prayer flags, showcasing the unique local culture and spirituality.

• Trek through diverse terrain, including subtropical forests, alpine meadows, glaciers, and river valleys.

Makalu Base Camp Trek 18-day  is a Himalayan adventure through remote villages, diverse landscapes, Makalu Barun National Park, and stunning mountain scenery.

• Explore the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang, the former kingdom of Mustang.

  • Visit Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and the royal palace.

  • Discover the sky caves of Chhoser, carved into cliffs centuries ago.

  • Experience the unique desert landscapes and barren cliffs of Upper Mustang.

  • Interact with the local Tibetan-influenced culture and traditions.

  • Walk through remote villages like Kagbeni, Chele, Syangboche, Ghami, and Tsarang.

  • Witness breathtaking high-altitude desert scenery and panoramic Himalayan views.

  • Enjoy two nights of cultural immersion in Lo Manthang.

Today is an important acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. You can take a short hike to the Everest View Hotel or nearby viewpoints for excellent views of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other Himalayan peaks. After breakfast, the trail begins with beautiful mountain views and gradually separates from the main Everest Base Camp route. Today’s trek is shorter but the altitude continues to increase. The trail climbs gradually through open valleys, yak grazing areas, and small settlements such as Luza and Lhafarma. You will enjoy wide mountain landscapes and peaceful surroundings throughout the day. Machhermo is a beautiful village located below rocky hills and snow-capped peaks. Today you will trek towards the beautiful Gokyo Valley, one of the most scenic destinations in the Everest region. The trail gradually climbs through high alpine landscapes with views of Cho Oyu and surrounding peaks. On the way, you will pass the first and second Gokyo Lakes before reaching the main Gokyo village beside the stunning third lake, Dudh Pokhari. The blue lake, mountain reflections, and peaceful setting make Gokyo one of the most beautiful places in the Himalayas.

Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and the massive Ngozumpa Glacier. The sunrise view from Gokyo Ri is truly unforgettable. The trail descends gradually through the same high-altitude landscapes, passing lakes, yak pastures, and small mountain settlements. You will again pass Phortse Tenga and Mong La before joining the main route back to Namche. The walk offers beautiful views of Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and other peaks. This is the final trekking day of the Gokyo Valley Trek. The trail descends steeply from Namche Bazaar towards the Dudh Koshi River and continues through familiar villages, forests, and suspension bridges. You will pass Monjo, Phakding, and other small settlements before climbing gradually back to Lukla. Gokyo Valley Trek is a 14-day Himalayan adventure featuring turquoise lakes, Sherpa villages, Gokyo Ri, and stunning Everest region views.

• Explore the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang
  • Travel through Nepal's restricted Upper Mustang region
  • Experience authentic Tibetan Buddhist culture
  • Visit ancient monasteries, palaces, and cave settlements

  • Drive through dramatic desert landscapes and colorful cliffs
  • Visit the sacred Muktinath Temple
  • Scenic journey through the Kali Gandaki Valley
  • Comfortable travel by private 4WD jeep
  • Beautiful mountain views of Nilgiri, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Mustang Himal

  • Two nights hotel accommodation in Pokhara with breakfast
